channel.description: RSS feed for with the latest articles

item.title: Harvard Returns Two Skulls Likely Belonging to Enslaved Individuals, More Than 150 Years After They Were Taken From Brazil for Eugenics Studies
item.description: The remains were welcomed back in solemn ceremonies in Rio de Janeiro and Salvador after years of pressure from researchers, community groups and the Brazilian government. One skull likely belonged to an individual who fought and died in an 1835 slave revolt

item.title: See the Rare Baby Rhinoceros Born at England's Chester Zoo, an Adorable Boost for Its Vulnerable Species
item.description: The calf, born October 11, is in good health and exploring a secluded paddock with its mother, out of view of the public

item.title: The NIH Has Decided to Move Its Last Group of Retired Research Chimpanzees to an Animal Sanctuary Next Year
item.description: The agency had previously determined that the animals were too old or ill for the journey. But a recent transfer involving another federally supported research facility pushed the National Institutes of Health to revisit the issue

item.title: Have Archaeologists Finally Pieced Together the 'Parthenon Puzzle,' One of Ancient Greece's Greatest Mysteries?
item.description: Centuries ago, the Parthenon's east pediment was reduced to rubble. German researchers now believe they have recreated the 39-figure scene depicting the birth of Athena with the help of Roman sarcophagi and 3D printers

item.title: This Self-Charging Toothbrush Has Bristles That Generate Electricity to Help Kill Bacteria That Cause Cavities and Gum Disease
item.description: In a short clinical trial, participants who used the experimental toothbrush reported less plaque, gum inflammation and bleeding than those who used traditional nylon-bristled brushes. However, more research is required to assess the tool's safety and efficacy

item.title: This Philosopher Was One of the First People to Donate His Body to Science. Nearly 200 Years Later, Researchers Are Still Learning From It
item.description: Jeremy Bentham, the founder of utilitarianism, had his corpse publicly dissected and turned into an "auto-icon," a lifelike display featuring his skeleton dressed in one of his suits

item.title: The North Atlantic Right Whale Population Has Shrunk, Raising Concerns About the Future of the Critically Endangered Species
item.description: The massive marine mammals are dying from ship strikes, fishing gear entanglements and other causes, which is affecting the species' ability to grow its numbers. The animals were hunted to the brink of extinction around 100 years ago

item.title: When a Dog Attacked a Group of Young Boys in 1885, It Sent Them on a Trans-Atlantic Adventure That Changed Medicine
item.description: A case of rabies was often fatal in the era before Louis Pasteur developed a vaccine. For the young patients to see the French doctor, though, required a new kind of collective effort

item.title: Readers Respond to the November Issue
item.description: Your feedback on the retirement of Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie G. Bunch III, the excavation of a Maya metropolis in Belize, and the intersection of art and astronomy

item.title: As Scandinavian Countries Slowly Converted to Christianity, Crusades Often Took on the Form of Viking Raids
item.description: A new book by historian Thomas Williams closes the gap between the two cultures and brings some otherwise unfamiliar medieval figures and events to life
